solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Perverse aristocrat picked up irreparably damaged car (5-3)

indicatorNotes.picked up: what a radio or an ear picks up is a sound, so the letters come from how the words are said

blocks.note: a toff is a posh person
run the two words together and the T slides across the gap

annotation.surface: A contrary nobleman who has been heard wrecking a car beyond repair.
annotation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person. The join moves when spoken: WRY TOFF becomes WRITE OFF.
annotation.definitionFit: Insurers' term: a car too damaged to be worth repairing is written off, so it is a write-off.

entries.clue: Curt chat after port wine (5)

indicatorNotes.Curt: curt means cut short, so JAW loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.after: the chat comes after the port

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian port

annotation.surface: A brusque conversation over a glass of port.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Port wine' reads as one drink; the definition is only 'wine', and 'port' is a harbour city.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Spanish region of La Rioja gives its name to its red and white wines.

entries.clue: One filling up catheter following treatment having beneficial effect (11)

indicatorNotes.filling: the I fills the space inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.following treatment: after treatment the letters of CATHETER UP are rearranged

annotation.surface: A nurse fitting a catheter after a successful course of treatment.
annotation.walkthrough: The hospital surface makes 'treatment' look medical; here it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, from the Greek for healing: a remedy that does you good is therapeutic.

entries.clue: Where actors may often be working blind (2-6)

blocks.note: a machine that is working is on
a window blind is a screen

annotation.surface: Performers who rehearse without being able to see.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blind' reads as unable to see; it is the kind that covers a window.
annotation.definitionFit: Film and television actors spend their working lives being seen on a screen.

entries.clue: One who’ll benefit from clients’ losses (7,8)

annotation.definition: One who’ll benefit from clients’ losses

blocks.note: reads as someone profiting, like a broker or a bookmaker
the losses are bereavements, not money: the clients have lost a relative

annotation.surface: A cynical broker who profits when customers lose money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Losses' suggests money lost on investments; here it means deaths, and the one paid for them is an undertaker.
annotation.definitionFit: An undertaker's business comes from families who have lost someone, so their loss is his income.

entries.clue: Stall China’s foreign correspondent? (3,3)

blocks.note: a stall or pen for animals
china = mate, from rhyming slang 'china plate'

annotation.surface: A newspaper correspondent reporting from China who is holding things up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so a pal. The question mark flags that 'foreign correspondent' is not a journalist here.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a pen pal is often abroad and exchanges letters, so is a foreign correspondent.

entries.clue: Silver-lined set of seals perhaps on entrance to Asian temple (6)

indicatorNotes.lined: the silver lines the inside of the pod
indicatorNotes.entrance to: the entrance of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a pod is a group of seals or whales
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: A pack of seals decorated with silver at the gateway to an Asian shrine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Asian temple' looks like the definition, but 'Asian' only supplies its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a pagoda is the tiered tower temple of Buddhist East Asia.

entries.clue: Buff barrel from the bottom up (3)

indicatorNotes.from the bottom up: in a down entry, reading from the bottom up turns the word round

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask

annotation.surface: Polishing a barrel starting at its base.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buff' looks like a verb, to polish; it is a noun, an enthusiast.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonyms for an enthusiast: a film buff is a film nut.

entries.clue: Foul-smelling substance in raised opening under a metal box (9)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down entry, raising a word reads it from the bottom up
indicatorNotes.under: in a down entry, this piece sits below the other

blocks.note: a safe is a strong metal box
an adit is a mine entrance

annotation.surface: Something smelly found in a hole beneath a metal strongbox.
annotation.walkthrough: An adit is a horizontal entrance into a mine, a crossword favourite.
annotation.definitionFit: Asafetida, a plant resin used as a spice, is notorious for its sulphurous stink.

entries.clue: Cards, one way or another? (6)

blocks.note: playing cards with a jester on them
surface padding that tells you to read 'Cards' in two ways

annotation.walkthrough: One word read two ways, as the tail of the clue says: pasteboard cards, and people who are a card, that is funny.
annotation.definitionFit: A pack's jokers are extra cards, and a person who is a card is a joker, a wag.

entries.clue: Singer, poor thing, mostly grates (8)

indicatorNotes.poor: a poor thing is in bad shape, so its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: JARS = grates, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A singer whose poor voice is mostly grating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is the definition: a songbird, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: any songbird is a singer, and the nightjar is known for its churring night song.

entries.clue: Eastern prince is open in retrospect (4)

indicatorNotes.in retrospect: looking back, so the word is read backwards

annotation.surface: A prince from the East who is candid looking back on things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Open' reads as candid, a trait of the prince; it is a door standing slightly open.
annotation.definitionFit: Raja is the Hindi title for a ruler, from the Sanskrit for king, used across India.

entries.clue: Note soldiers having again stepped back where monk would have gone (10)

indicatorNotes.stepped back: back turns the preceding letters round

blocks.note: re, the second note of the scale

annotation.surface: A musician rejoining the army ranks and retracing their steps.
annotation.walkthrough: A reredorter was the latrine block of a medieval monastery, sited behind the dorter, the monks' dormitory.
annotation.definitionFit: Euphemism: where a monk would have gone is the toilet, and the reredorter was the monastery's.

entries.clue: Echo and the Bunnymen, initially playing around Queen, once hosted by legendary US patriot (11)

indicatorNotes.initially: only the first letter of Bunnymen
indicatorNotes.around: one thing around another encircles it, so AT is placed either side of ER
indicatorNotes.hosted by: a host takes guests in, so REVERE takes the rest inside it

blocks.note: Paul Revere, of the midnight ride of 1775

annotation.surface: The Liverpool band Echo and the Bunnymen playing before a queen at an old American hero's house.
annotation.walkthrough: The band name is broken up: 'Echo' is the definition, and only the B of Bunnymen is used. Two nested containers: one inside another, all inside the patriot.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: a sound that echoes round a hall reverberates.

entries.clue: Heavenly ale, there after cycling (8)

indicatorNotes.after cycling: cycling moves letters from the front round to the back

blocks.note: move AL from the front to the back

annotation.surface: Wonderful beer waiting at the end of a bike ride.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly ale' reads as praise for the beer; 'Heavenly' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: ethereal comes from ether, the upper air of the heavens.

entries.clue: Small group of working mothers network operator blocks (9)

indicatorNotes.working: the letters of MOTHERS are worked into a new order
indicatorNotes.blocks: EE sits in the middle, blocking the way

blocks.note: EE is a British mobile phone network

annotation.surface: A few working mums blocked by their phone company.
annotation.walkthrough: EE is a UK mobile network, one of the big four.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a group of three people is about as small as a group gets.

entries.clue: Useless short film assumes nothing (4)

indicatorNotes.short: VIDEO cut short loses its end
indicatorNotes.assumes: to assume is to take on, so VID takes O inside

annotation.surface: A pointless brief clip that takes nothing for granted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Assumes' reads as supposes; it means takes on, puts inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal sense: a void contract has no force, so it is useless.

entries.clue: In America, can all others prepare to ditch leader (4,4)

annotation.surface: A question whether Americans can get everyone else ready to dump their boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a verb; it is American slang for a toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional use: in the US a public toilet is a restroom, and a can is slang for one.

entries.clue: Legal document with brief’s about right (4)

indicatorNotes.brief: WITH made brief loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.about: to go about something is to surround it, so WIT is placed either side of R

annotation.surface: A legal document and a barrister's opinion that it is roughly correct.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like a lawyer, fitting the legal surface; it only tells you to shorten WITH. The 's is 'is', read as the link.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a writ is the court's written order, such as a summons.

entries.clue: Periodically cut out biccies and pick dessert (3,5)

indicatorNotes.Periodically cut out: every other letter is removed, at regular intervals

blocks.note: bIcCiEs with the odd letters removed
the pick of the crop is the cream

annotation.surface: Skipping biscuits now and then and choosing a pudding instead.
annotation.walkthrough: Biccies is British slang for biscuits, that is cookies.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: ice cream is among the commonest sweet courses served after a meal.

entries.clue: Ford in the past called perjurer, shunning Republicans (6)

indicatorNotes.shunning: the Rs are shunned, left out

blocks.note: rang = called on the phone, then without R
a perjurer lies under oath, then without R
R = Republican, two of them removed

annotation.surface: A former US president, Gerald Ford, branded a perjurer and avoiding his own party.
annotation.walkthrough: Ford looks like the president; it is the carmaker, whose Anglia was a small British family car of the 1940s to 1960s.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Anglia is a discontinued Ford car model, hence 'in the past'.

entries.clue: Caught kid maybe going down (10)

indicatorNotes.Caught: a sound caught by the ear

blocks.note: a kid is one example of offspring; the two spellings differ in one vowel

annotation.surface: A child being caught and sent down.
annotation.walkthrough: The noun with an A means offspring; the adjective with an E means descending.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym from Latin descendere, to go down: a descendent path is going down.

entries.clue: Leave X-ray to be checked by electronic form of tech (4)

indicatorNotes.to be checked by: checked means held in, so X is contained

blocks.note: X-ray is X in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: An X-ray being reviewed by some electronic technology.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Checked' reads as examined, as an X-ray would be; it means held back or restrained.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs, and the stage direction: an actor told to exit leaves the stage.

entries.clue: State bore recalled interrupting Nixon intermittently (5)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so the word is turned round
indicatorNotes.interrupting: breaks into the middle of IO
indicatorNotes.intermittently: something intermittent comes and goes, so letters are taken and skipped in turn

annotation.surface: A dull state official remembered for cutting in on President Nixon now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person; it is the past tense of bear.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Idaho is one of the fifty US states, in the north-west.

entries.clue: Could it screen one who is lying? (8)

annotation.definition: Could it screen one who is lying?

blocks.note: reads as vetting, like a lie-detector test; it means cover, shield
reads as a liar; it is someone lying in bed

annotation.surface: Wondering whether a lie detector could screen out a liar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests dishonesty and 'screen' vetting; the thing that screens someone lying down is a bed cover.
annotation.definitionFit: A coverlet is a bedspread, which covers and so screens whoever is lying beneath it.

entries.clue: Section of Weekend supplement (3)

indicatorNotes.Section of: a section is a piece taken from inside the words

annotation.surface: Part of a Sunday paper's magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supplement' reads as a newspaper magazine; it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to eke out a small income is to add to it bit by bit, from an old word for increase.

entries.clue: Lamb’s heart also complex, like a ruminant’s stomach (6)

annotation.surface: A lamb's heart and stomach described like offal on a butcher's slab.
annotation.walkthrough: The omasum is the third chamber of a ruminant's stomach; omasal is its adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical adjective: the omasum is a chamber of a cud-chewer's stomach, and omasal describes it.

entries.clue: Retaliate about shifting grand city in Europe (6)

indicatorNotes.shifting: the G is shifted to the front

annotation.surface: Taking revenge for money being moved around a European city.
annotation.walkthrough: The G sits second in the reversed word and has to be moved to the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Geneva, on Lake Geneva, is Switzerland's second city.

entries.clue: Refrain in sea-shanties, odd half-hearted shout (8)

indicatorNotes.half-hearted: BELLOW has two Ls at its heart; half of them goes

blocks.note: a bellow is a shout, then minus one L

annotation.surface: Sailors singing a chorus with a strange feeble yell.
annotation.walkthrough: Rum meaning odd is British. The refrain is an old, rare word.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a nonsense chorus word sung by sailors, like yo-heave-ho, found in dictionaries as rumbelow.
